subject: Porting/interop readiness: Acme evaluation — next tests & demo follow-up
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@acme.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Porting/interop readiness: Acme evaluation — next tests & demo follow-up

Hi Simon / team,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the high-level goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short POC window: 

Key takeaways from call:
- Goal: evaluate porting risk + performance for moving inference from current hyperscaler stack to a mix of Redwood-hosted and dedicated capacity; primary concerns were API compatibility, prompt diffs, latency and security controls (VPC/data residency).
- Primary workloads: multi-turn customer chat (avg 600 tokens), batch embeddings for search, and a reranking pipeline.
- Security: need SOC2 evidence, ability to bring keys (KMS) and optional VPC peering for private deployment.

Proposed next tests (short sprint, 2 weeks):
1) OpenAI-compat smoke: run 20 representative prompts (chat + structured completion) through Redwood’s API using your existing SDK calls to surface prompt diffs and tokenization differences.
2) Latency/throughput: 95th/99th percentile token latencies for a quantized LLM vs your current hyperscaler; include cold-start and KV-cache warmed runs.
3) SDK swap sample: provide guidelines and a small code patch for replacing current OpenAI client usage with Redwood SDK (node/python examples).
4) Security checklist deliverable: SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integration notes, and VPC deployment options.

Action items / owners (suggested):
- Acme: share 20 sample prompts (anonymized) + 1 representative long chat transcript — Simon (by 2027-04-24)
- Redwood: run OpenAI-compat smoke and deliver diff report — Sergio & Rishi (by 2027-05-06)
- Redwood: produce SDK swap guide and short demo session — Neha (demo week of 2027-05-10)
- Redwood: assemble SOC2 + infra notes — Olga (by 2027-05-03)

I attached a one-page evaluation plan (acme-eval-plan.xlsx) with timing and a proposed demo agenda. If that timeline looks OK I’ll lock times for the compatibility smoke test and the SDK demo.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: acme-eval-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-22T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Porting/interop readiness: Acme evaluation — next tests & demo follow-up

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear summary. That plan looks good and I can confirm the timeline in general. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Security: we absolutely need SOC2 Type II evidence and a clear KMS/HSM path because our data residency policy requires customer-managed keys for PII. Also would like to understand network topology options (VPC peering vs private endpoint).
2) For the OpenAI-compat smoke — can you include 2 prompt templates that are known to be fragile (few-shot with numbered line prompts)? Those are where we saw big deltas before.
3) Procurement: I’ve looped in procurement@acme.com — they’ll send an NDA/PO template if needed.

I’ll share the anonymized prompt set and a long chat transcript by 2027-04-24. Attached is our internal priorities doc so you can prioritize the test matrix (acme-interop-priority.pdf).

Simon
Head of ML Platform | Acme Corp
simon.lewis@acme.com

Attachment: acme-interop-priority.pdf (pdf)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@acme.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-23T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Porting/interop readiness: Acme evaluation — next tests & demo follow-up

Simon / team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the priority doc. We’ll scope the tests as follows: 

OpenAI-compat smoke (owner: Rishi)
- Run your 20 prompts against: (a) your current hyperscaler endpoint, (b) Redwood API with OpenAI-compatible surface, and (c) Redwood dedicated instance with same model variant.
- Produce a diff summary highlighting tokenization differences, sample outputs that diverge, and a small set of reproducible prompts that cause behavior changes.

Latency suite (owner: Sergio)
- 95th/99th percentile token response times for 600-token multi-turn chat. Tests: cold start, warmed KV-cache, and batched short requests. Compare against your reported performance on GCP and AWS.

SDK swap POC (owner: Neha)
- Two short examples (Node + Python) showing minimal code changes and error-handling differences. Also include a table of surface differences (param names, streaming behavior, function-calling mapping).

Security artifacts (owner: Olga)
- SOC2 excerpt, KMS integration notes, and VPC deployment patterns.

Timing: we’ll start the smoke tests once we have your prompt set (submit by 2027-04-24). Expect the first deliverable (compat diff + quick findings) by 2027-05-06. Demo week as suggested the week of 2027-05-10; we can do a 45-min technical demo + 30-min Q&A.

Related links: HubSpot deal RDW-ACME-2027-01 and a shared Drive folder (links included below).

Sergio
Director, Solution Engineering | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
